rounds.question: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index: by how much will the seasonally adjusted CPI-U index for rent of primary residence, US city average (series CUSR0000SEHA), change from the month before to November 2026, in percent, computed from the two published index levels (not the one-decimal figure in the BLS press table)? The series is smooth: the ranked reference, the mean of the six latest one-month changes, has missed by about 0.06 points on average since mid-2023. The release is scheduled for 2026-12-10 at 08:30 ET (date from third-party calendars and the owner doc; bls.gov was not readable).
rounds.resolve: 100 x (L_M / L_M-1 - 1) for M = November 2026, both CUSR0000SEHA index levels taken from the first BLS Public Data API response archived under sources/bls_cpi/ at or after the 08:30 ET release whose newest period is M; never rounded, and later revisions (including the February seasonal re-estimation) never change it. A release cancelled, delayed past release + 45 days, or a missing M-1 level cancels the round; it is never built from a two-month change.
